diffs.diff: acceleration_g: datasheet reading gives 0.0000625 per count, the part's model has 0.98, 0.98, 0.98
diffs.evidence: The model gives milli-g per 12-bit count (raw 16-bit >> 4) x 0.98 mg, i.e. 0.98/16 = 0.06125 mg = 0.00006125 g per raw 16-bit count. The second reading used the approximate 1 mg/digit (0.0000625 g per raw count), about 2% off and in g not mg. ST's official LSM303AGR driver (lsm303agr_reg.c): 'float_t lsm303agr_from_fs_2g_hr_to_mg(int16_t lsb) { return ((float_t)lsb / 16.0f) * 0.98f; }', which matches datasheet Table 3 (So = 0.98 mg/LSB at FS=±2 g, high-resolution mode). The model's register setup (CTRL_REG4_A = 0x88: ±2 g, HR) matches that row.

diffs.diff: magnetic_field_gauss: datasheet reading gives 0.0015 per count, the part's model has 0.98, 0.98, 0.98
diffs.evidence: The magnetometer is the sub-device at 0x1E. Its sim.subDevices measures (0x68/0x6A/0x6C) use scale 1.5 in mgauss, and the driver uses MAG_MG_PER_LSB = 1.5. 1.5 mgauss = 0.0015 gauss per count, the same value in different units. The gate lists only the accelerometer's 0.98 scales because it does not read subDevices. ST's official driver: 'float_t lsm303agr_from_lsb_to_mgauss(int16_t lsb) { return (float_t)lsb * 1.5f; }'. WHO_AM_I_M 0x4F = 0x40 (LSM303AGR_ID_MG) also matches the model.
